question.problem:
Several children were asked how many siblings they have. The number of siblings of each child was recorded below. If $X$ is the number of siblings of a randomly selected child, what is the expected value of $X?$

| Number of siblings | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of Children | $1$ | $5$ | $3$ | $1$ |
question.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

We're given the frequencies of the number of siblings, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of children is $1+5+3+1=10,$ so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0)=f(0) & =\frac{1}{10} \\ P(X=1)=f(1) & =\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2} \\ P(X=2)=f(2) & =\frac{3}{10} \\ P(X=3)=f(3) & =\frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

We organize these results in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{10}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{3}{10}$ | $\frac{1}{10}$ |

Now, summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{10})+1(\frac{1}{2})+2(\frac{3}{10})+3(\frac{1}{10}) \\  & =0+\frac{5}{10}+\frac{6}{10}+\frac{3}{10} \\  & =\frac{0+5+6+3}{10} \\  & =\frac{14}{10} \\  & =1.4\,.\end{aligned}
$$
